items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: I realized then that Louis really liked me, and our friendship lasted forever.

ctx.x: Oh it was terrific. I realized then that Louis really liked me, and our friendship lasted forever. He used to call up and say, “Hey I’m laying off a couple of days, come on out to the house and bring your brother with you,” because he loved my brother too.
Now you said Miles said the same thing to you.

items.title: Avakian George — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: neither of us ever dreaming that I would ever be his record producer and that we would become fast, beautiful friends

ctx.x: What a beautiful picture that is.

On top of which, he’s expressing himself to me, a relative stranger, just somebody who had discovered these records and turned out to be a fan of his, neither of us ever dreaming that I would ever be his record producer and that we would become fast, beautiful friends, see each other abroad, be with our wives and all that, having dinner, etc. That was a marvelous relationship. I haven’t even talked about the relationship with Duke, which is different, because Duke was . . .
